versions.changelog:
## New features
- Selectable recording backend: Choose TVHeadend DVR or Jellyfin DVR in plugin settings. TVHeadend remains the default; Jellyfin DVR uses Jellyfin’s scheduler and configured recording directory.
- Multiple TVHeadend servers: Jellyfin DVR mode supports separate native tuners and guide providers for each server, registered automatically without manual channel mapping.
- Connection testing: Test unsaved connection settings for HTSP, HTTP ticket and HTTP Basic streaming, with results for connection, authentication and stream-access failures.
- Programme thumbnails: Optionally generate missing artwork from buffered video on watched HTSP channels.
- Background thumbnails: A separate option captures unwatched channels at low priority while no HTSP playback readers are active. Captures are limited to one channel per minute.
- Channel tags: Import TVHeadend channel tags into Jellyfin, including tag renames and deletions.
- Track languages: Preserve audio and subtitle languages, normalize language codes consistently, and fill missing languages from stream probing.
## Playback and performance improvements
- Enrich HTSP stream metadata with broadcast frame rate and aspect ratio, plus probed interlacing, HDR, bit depth, codec profile and bitrate.
- Probe existing buffered video without opening another tuner subscription. Cache results and retain broadcast metadata if probing fails.
- Reduce startup round trips by skipping unused disk-space and server-time queries on playback connections.
- Lower warm subscriptions to idle priority after the last viewer leaves and restore playback priority when reused.
- Isolate shared streams by server, account and profile, preventing equal channel numbers on different servers from sharing the wrong stream.
- Cache native channel listings to avoid repeating failed-server waits during every programme lookup.
- Group background thumbnail captures by learned mux identity while ensuring every eligible channel gets a turn.
## Guide, artwork and recording improvements
- Read programme data from HTSP event pushes instead of repeatedly requesting each channel’s guide.
- Handle partial updates, deletions and reconnect snapshots in guide and channel caches.
- Coalesce and throttle guide refreshes to avoid unnecessary full rebuilds.
- Fetch TVHeadend image-cache artwork through HTSP, with authenticated HTTP fallback when HTSP file access is unavailable.
- Refresh generated thumbnails after five minutes and overlay cached channel logos when available.
- Preserve broadcaster artwork and keep channels available when artwork downloads fail or time out.
- Refresh recording listings after DVR changes without invalidating caches for duplicate pushes.
- Track recording modification timestamps and retain cached recording artwork after its programme leaves the EPG.
- Authenticate native HTTP recording streams through TVHeadend ticket URLs, compatible with Jellyfin’s TS recorder.
- Preserve native tuner IDs during server edits and remove generated native dashboard entries when switching back to TVHeadend DVR.
- Show the active recording backend and per-server connection and streaming information in plugin status.

- Note integration of upstream plugin v15 while retaining the fork’s HTSP enhancements.
- Describe improved cleanup of deferred HTSP streaming resources.
- Mention that completed guide-image download tasks are now removed to prevent unnecessary accumulation.
- Highlight the move to xUnit and expanded shared-streaming, cancellation, and cleanup regression coverage.
- Explain that Release builds now provide a versioned ZIP containing `TVHeadEnd.dll`, suitable for a Jellyfin repository; the DLL remains available for manual installation.
- State compatibility with Jellyfin 12 and .NET 10.
